brief: A sturdy step for my toddler to stand on so they can reach the bathroom sink.

requirements.requirement: A step for a toddler to stand on (flat, closed standing surface)
requirements.evidence: Solid top covers on the two front cells (-1,1,0 and 0,1,0) make an 80 mm first step. Solid top covers on the three back cells at level 1 make the 160 mm top step. Each surface is a full hex cell, about 190 mm wide, and caps close all open side edges so there are no open sides.

requirements.requirement: Height to reach the bathroom sink
requirements.evidence: The top step is 160 mm high and the lower step 80 mm. Whether that's enough depends on your sink height and your child's height, which the brief doesn't give. Another level could be added if more height is needed.

requirements.requirement: Sturdy: safely holds a toddler's weight without tipping or breaking
requirements.evidence: The shape helps: the base is wide (507 × 467 mm), every base-to-base wall is joint-bolted, solid bottom covers sit flat on the floor, and check_build reports no collisions. But the configurator checks only fit and collisions. It knows nothing about strength, load rating, the filament or print settings, or whether the stool tips, so I can't confirm it's safe to stand on. Test it with an adult's weight before a child uses it.

requirements.requirement: Safe for bathroom use (non-slip footing, standing on a wet floor or step)
requirements.evidence: The brief doesn't ask for this directly; it's implied by a bathroom step. The configurator has no non-slip feet or grip surfaces, and it can't judge slipperiness or water resistance. Add non-slip pads under the stool and grip tape on the steps yourself.

finish.summary: I built a two-tier step stool, 507 × 467 mm across and 160 mm tall. Its back row is three cells at levels 0 and 1, so the top step is 160 mm. Its front row is two cells at level 0, giving an 80 mm first step. All 9 walls between bases are joint-bolted together. The 5 standing tops and all 5 bottoms have solid covers, and 20 caps close every open side edge. check_build reports no issues and a clear mesh-collision check. The parts list is 55 parts: 8 bases, 3 snaps, 9 joint bolts, 10 covers and 25 caps. That's more than the usual modest size because the caps close every open side.

lines.label: Edge cap · female, two stories tall
Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
